one_liner: Tiny typeless C-like scripting language and abstract machine; 1.9x (C core) to 3.5x (x86 asm core) PUC Lua on recursive fib.
what_it_does: Pawn is an embeddable extension language with C-like syntax where every value is a 32-bit cell. Scripts are compiled ahead of time by a separate compiler (pawncc) into P-code (.amx files) that the host runs on the abstract machine (AMX) through a small C API: aux_LoadProgram/amx_Init, amx_Register for native functions, amx_Exec. It is not Lua-compatible and has no tables, closures or objects; it targets hosts that want a small, sandboxed script VM, down to ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers.
how_it_is_fast: Work is moved to compile time: pawncc resolves calls and variables statically and its peephole optimizer emits macro instructions (-O2) and packed opcodes with the operand folded into the opcode cell (-O3), so the VM executes fewer, typeless register-style instructions (PRI/ALT registers) with no type tags, hashing or garbage collection. Native calls are relocated to direct function pointers (SYSREQ.D). The fastest row uses the hand-written x86-32 assembler core (amxexec.asm, token threading); the portable C core in amx.c is a plain switch loop, and amxexec_gcc.c offers an indirect-threaded core via GCC labels-as-values.
when_to_use: Embedding a small, sandboxed script VM in a C/C++ host where scripts are integer- and call-heavy and a C-like syntax suits the script authors.
Microcontrollers and small devices: assembler cores exist for ARM7, Thumb-2 and ARMv6-M (Cortex-M0/M0+), and the 4.1 release documents running scripts from ROM.
Hosts that can compile scripts ahead of time and ship only bytecode plus the abstract machine, with scripts calling into host natives.
32-bit x86 hosts that can link the MASM/WASM/TASM (or NASM via amxexecn.asm) assembler core, where Scriptorium's 3.5x-over-Lua figure applies.
when_not_to_use: You need a dynamic language with tables, strings as first-class values, closures or GC: Pawn is typeless 32-bit cells with fixed-size arrays (the garbage collector is an optional module).

64-bit hosts that need 64-bit cells or 64-bit builds: open issues #77 (64-bit Windows -C64 builds run scripts into memory errors), #85 and #86 (master does not build on Linux x86_64, unresolved amx_jit_* symbols) were never fixed before the archive.
You want peak speed: in the same Scriptorium table LuaJIT (0.111 s), LuaJIT -joff (0.521 s), Terra, c4-jit and libtcc all beat both Pawn rows.
You need an actively maintained GitHub upstream: the repo was archived on 2025-09-26 and development moved to Codeberg (not checked here, blocked).

integration.form: source-drop (amx.c plus amxaux.c and optional extension modules compiled into the host; pawncc compiler as a separate executable; Windows DLL builds also provided)
integration.dependencies: none for the C core; an x86 assembler (MASM/WASM/TASM, or NASM for amxexecn.asm) for the x86 assembler core and JIT; GNU as for the ARM cores
integration.min_toolchain: ANSI C compiler (CMake setup lists Microsoft, Borland, OpenWatcom and GNU); amxexec_gcc.c needs GCC or Intel C/C++
integration.platforms: Win32 and Linux with 32-bit cells; x86-32 assembler core and JIT; ARM7, Thumb-2 and Cortex-M0 assembler cores; CMake forces i386 on macOS because of 64-bit issues
integration.thread_safety: not documented; all VM state is held in the per-script AMX structure passed to amx_Exec

gotchas: Harness flaws in the Scriptorium numbers: run.bat runs a bare `lua` resolved through PATH (the repo root has no lua.exe and lua/ holds only lua-5.3.1 and luajit-2.0 sources), so the PUC Lua binary, version and build behind the 1.341 s baseline are unrecorded; fib.lua declares fibR as a global, so every recursive Lua call pays a global-table lookup that Pawn's statically resolved CALL does not; bench.cc never checks program output (the scripts' comment 'Should return 433494437' is fib(43), not fib(34)).

The 3.5x figure needs the 32-bit x86 assembler core; Scriptorium built the portable C core with MSVC, where amx.c dispatches through a switch, and that row is 1.9x. An earlier batch in bench.csv shows only 1.44x (C core) and 3.3x (asm core) against Lua 2.36 s; the table keeps the per-row minimum.

JIT is incompatible with macro instructions, packed opcodes and overlays (amx.c turns them off under AMX_JIT), so -O3 scripts cannot use it; Scriptorium's JIT build failed (amxjitr.err) and has no row.

Licence: Apache-2.0 with a static-linking exception that applies only to unmodified Work distributed in Object form; amxexec_gcc.c carries its own zlib-style notice, and the documentation is CC BY-SA.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Pawn over Lua-family siblings (Luau, LuaJIT, Ravi) when the script language can be a typeless C-like dialect compiled ahead of time and the host is a 32-bit or microcontroller target that wants a tiny sandboxed VM; on desktop x86-64, Luau or LuaJIT give a full dynamic language and Daslang a typed one at higher speed, and in the same fib(34) table c4-jit (0.136 s) and Terra (0.121 s) are faster but are not small sandboxed VMs.
verified_claims_summary: r-lyeh's Scriptorium (2015, MSVC /Ox, AMD A10 3.8 GHz, Windows 7) timed whole-process runs of recursive fib(34), averaging 5 runs per batch and keeping the best batch: Pawn 4.0 (build 4733, script compiled with pawncc -O3) ran in 0.384 s on the x86-32 assembler core and 0.719 s on the C core, against 1.341 s for an unidentified PUC Lua binary found on PATH (about 3.5x and 1.9x, derived from page data). Both Pawn and Lua times come from the same batch (bench.csv lines 65-70); nothing checks that the programs printed the right result.
status_note: Archived on GitHub on 2025-09-26 after the 4.1.7152 release (2025-03-25), with development moved to Codeberg (activity there unchecked); Apache-2.0 with a static-linking exception and small enough to vendor, but 64-bit builds have open, unanswered bug reports.
